author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The British Museum opened its sold-out Bayeux Tapestry exhibition to the public Thursday, giving visitors in London a close view of the nearly 1,000-year-old embroidery.

The work has left France for the first time since the 11th century and is scheduled to remain at the museum for 10 months. Its stitched scenes depict the Norman invasion of England in 1066 and the events surrounding the Battle of Hastings, making it one of Europe’s best-known visual historical records.

The 70-meter tapestry is displayed in a purpose-built glass case. Ticket holders receive 40 minutes on an elevated platform before moving closer to examine the stitching. The museum’s arrangement is designed to show both the full narrative sequence and small details that are difficult to appreciate in reproductions.

Demand exhausted the available tickets before the public opening, and the exhibition has generated widespread attention across Britain. The loan is unusual because of the tapestry’s age, fragility and national significance in France. Its extended London stay gives scholars and museum visitors a rare chance to study the object outside its longtime home in Bayeux.

headline: Bayeux Tapestry opens sold-out London exhibition
